text:
[LTAC.9.1] **Declarative-only.** `after` lowers to a timer fact
plus a follow-up rule; no engine state changes, no
cancellation, no serialisation. Per-fact supersedure on
author-named keys (`as <expr>`) is the mechanism at
[LRST]; it preserves the declarative
core (the supersedure mechanism is the same as
[LCRS.6.2]). Pending `after`s
are not queued.

idris.name: ltac_3_3__survives_parent_retract_timed
idris.note: 'No cancellation': the parent's retraction withdraws no timer; only an `as` key would, which is not lowered. Executed. LESS than the clause: the supersedure mechanism is outside.

idris.name: ltac_9_1__nothing_before_the_delay_timed
idris.note: NOTHING BEFORE THE DELAY: the same program, the advance to 3 and a pump fire nothing, and the timer is live beside the trigger -- temporal/LTAC.9.3.runtime's shape (the runner prints no timer; the model holds it). Executed. LESS than the clause: no `as` key, so no supersedure is modelled; the declarative core alone.
